title: pvVisItSASReader
body:
## pvVisItSASReader

Reads binary Fortran SAS geometry and data files (.sasgeom with .sas/.sasdata): an unstructured mesh of assemblies and channels with cell arrays identifying each assembly and channel and a temperature field over time. The plugin source gives no further description of the producing code; ParaView has no other reader for it. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Keep the geometry and data files together; the data file alone has no mesh.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItSASReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItSASReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from SAS data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. For SAS data these are cell arrays "assembly_id", "assembly_type", "channel_id", "channel_type" and "temperature". | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single SAS file to read (.sasgeom, .sas, .sasdata); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Keep the .sasgeom geometry and the data files together. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The SAS plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the SAS meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The SAS plugin reports one unstructured mesh of assemblies and channels; take the name from the reader's available list. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from SAS data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The SAS plugin declares its variables zone-centred, so this list normally stays empty. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItSASReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
